#!/bin/sh
set -eu

base=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")/.." && pwd)
lock_file="$base/.reconcile.lock"

# A kernel-held advisory lock disappears automatically if this process exits,
# including when it is interrupted.  The file itself is only the lock anchor.
exec 9>"$lock_file"
if ! flock -n 9; then
  printf '%s\n' 'reconcile: another invocation already owns the job; no work performed' >&2
  exit 75
fi

while IFS= read -r batch || [ -n "$batch" ]; do
  [ -n "$batch" ] || continue
  if grep -Fqx -- "$batch" "$base/ledger.tsv"; then
    continue
  else
    status=$?
    if [ "$status" -ne 1 ]; then
      printf '%s\n' 'reconcile: unable to read ledger.tsv' >&2
      exit "$status"
    fi
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$batch" >> "$base/ledger.tsv"
done < "$base/pending.tsv"

chown --reference=bin/reconcile "$tmp"
